title: Ordinary-PR CI critical path: strategy experiment ledger
method: Each strategic hypothesis was tried as an experiment against real soldr evidence (GitHub run/job API, CI logs, local bosn runs, a real-runner probe on an experiment branch, and simulations calibrated against measured runs). Pros/cons are evidence, not opinion; every figure names its source.

baseline.window: soldr CI, 2026-09-25 .. 2026-10-02: 230 pull_request runs, 100 main push runs, 80 merged PRs

pr_ci_wall_seconds.source: successful pull_request CI runs, first job start to last job end

linux_x64_breakdown.source: 12 PR runs' step timings; run 36954283026 log

hypotheses.name: Trust the local gate's attestation (skip remote quick-gate jobs on attested PRs)
hypotheses.experiment: E1: replay soldr's 80 merged PRs: eligibility by changed files, merge verdicts before/after the gate, main post-merge failures, and which steps of the would-be-skipped jobs ever failed.

results.eligible_refined_only_skip_job_closure: 62/80 (78%); 18 ineligible touch ci.yml, _build-and-test.yml, actions, gate scripts or the CI-only probe scripts
results.docs_only_already_skipped: 0 of the 80 (docs-only PRs are rare; path-selection already handles them)
results.remote_only_steps_that_ever_failed: none: all 4 Linux x64 failures were the ci-test step, all 5 Lint failures were lint-lane steps (Python tests, ruff, spawn-path guard) -- all covered locally
results.pre_gate_no_attestation: 9 main breakages in one day (2026-09-26), every one from a PR merged with a cancelled or red PR run
results.post_gate: 5/5 PRs attested and green on first push; 0 main failures
results.critical_path_if_trusted: CI mode (~15 s + full-history fetch) and CI path selection (~14 s): ~14 min -> ~1 min

pros: Removes the entire ~14 min wait for ~78% of PRs, with no extra runners
Remote jobs rerun the exact command the gate ran (GATE-001), so they add latency, not evidence, on an attested head
Cuts PR runner minutes (~11 runner-min per eligible PR)
Makes the cheap required check honest: merging no longer races a 14-min run (pre-gate: 14/75 merged without a green run)
cons: The trailer is an honesty contract, not a proof (anyone can type it)
PR head is tested, not the merge result: merge skew reaches main
Linux x64 is not a pure mirror: CI-only probes would only run post-merge
Local and CI environments differ (cores, env, network); timing-sensitive tests can pass locally and fail remotely
A PR could weaken its own gate and then attest against it
hypotheses.verdict: ADOPT, as GATE-008 with the round-3 safeguards (base-branch policy, surfaces, exact attestation, audit sample, mandatory post-merge run).

hypotheses.name: Run only affected tests: crate-graph selection
hypotheses.experiment: E2: map each of the 80 PRs' changed files to workspace packages (soldr cargo metadata), take reverse-dependency closures, weight by per-package CI test-seconds from run 36954283026; GATE-007's audited tests-lane exclusions decide what is irrelevant; anything unowned runs everything.

results.no_rust_tests_needed: 22/80 (already skipped locally by the GATE-007 tests-lane cache)
results.subset: 31/80, but every subset selects >= 96% of test-seconds
results.mean_test_seconds_selected: 71% -- and 0% of the savings lands on a subset PR
results.why: soldr-cli holds 1,846 of 1,933 test-seconds (95%) and reverse-depends on every other crate

pros: Would help a repository with independent crates
cons: ~0 marginal benefit on soldr: the only PRs it saves are ones the lane cache already skips
Per-test selection (coverage + runtime file reads) is the only real lever and is expensive and unproven; soldr's slow tests spawn the whole soldr binary, so each covers most of it
hypotheses.verdict: DEFER for soldr. Keep #191 as a fleet option for multi-crate repositories; per-test recording only after shadow data justifies it.

hypotheses.name: Smart cache inheritance (setup-soldr key: auto, nearest-ancestor restore)
hypotheses.experiment: E3: PR vs main Linux x64 step timings (12 runs each) and cache hit lines in the PR log.

results.pr_linux_median_vs_main: 647 s vs 692 s (PRs are not slower)
results.pr_zccache_hit_rate: 100% (restore-key prefix already inherits main's newest entry)
results.latency_upside_on_pr_critical_path: <= 30-60 s, and 0 once H1 skips the job

pros: Correct ancestor (not merely newest) restore on divergent branches
Fewer, shared cache entries: the cache-budget verdict failed 52 runs in the window (27 PR, 25 main)
Helps main/ci-full/release runs, which still compile
cons: No measurable PR latency win today
hypotheses.verdict: KEEP AS HYGIENE, not a latency lever: reframe #185 around cache-budget failures.

hypotheses.name: Make the tests themselves faster (remote-only per-test cost)
hypotheses.experiment: E4: local bosn probe (5 cheap cargo_front_door tests: as-is / CI env vars / 4 CPUs) then a real-runner probe on an experiment branch (run 36964344956) with environment variants and strace. Second real-runner probe (run 36965017158): SOLDR_MANIFEST_DISABLE=1 and 4-wide variants.

results.local_bosn: 0.2-1.0 s per test in every variant (CI env vars and 4 CPUs change nothing)
results.real_runner_alone: 3.8-4.1 s per test (plain nextest, -j1); repeat run identical
results.strace: every test opens connections to zackees.github.io (toolchain catalogue) and raw.githubusercontent.com; no syscall >= 1 s; ~2.6 s summed clock_nanosleep
results.decomposition: ~5 s per test is the catalogue fetch; the remaining in-DAG excess (to 10-15 s) is contention while compile/Dylint stages overlap
results.real_runner_alone_run2: 5.1-5.4 s per cheap test; dylint test 11.6 s
results.manifest_disabled: 0.17-0.22 s per cheap test (30x); dylint test 6.6 s
results.four_wide: 5.6 s per cheap test with the catalogue lookup, 0.17-0.22 s without -- concurrency adds little once the lookup is gone
results.root_cause: each fixture's fresh SOLDR_CACHE_DIR makes the soldr front door fetch the toolchain catalogue (zackees.github.io/soldr-toolchain/catalogue.v1.json + raw.githubusercontent.com parts) over the runner's network: ~5 s per test, x127 cargo_front_door tests = the ~604 s CI-vs-local gap

pros: One-line class of fix: the shared test fixture disables the catalogue lookup (tests needing it opt back in), which also makes the suite hermetic (no live network per test)
Helps every remaining remote run: main push, ci-full, release gate, non-trusted PRs
Simulated: removing the per-test excess takes nextest 483 -> 240 s with no extra runners
cons: Does not remove the PR wait by itself (Linux x64 ~11.5 -> ~7 min estimated)
hypotheses.verdict: ADOPT as soldr#3530: disable the catalogue lookup in the shared fixture; measured 30x on the affected tests.

hypotheses.name: Shard nextest across runners
hypotheses.experiment: E5: nextest scheduling simulation with real per-test durations and test-group caps (docs/designs/experiments/pr_critical_path_shardsim.py), calibrated 483 s simulated vs ~480 s measured.
pros: ~3 min off Linux x64 at N=2 for every remote run
cons: Adds runners and ~1.5 runner-min of setup per shard per run
hypotheses.verdict: REJECT for now; revisit only if main/release test stages stay > ~4 min after H4.

hypotheses.name: Larger runners
hypotheses.experiment: Local 4-CPU probe (taskset -c 0-3) and the real-runner probe: the slow tests are not CPU-bound.
cons: Paid (standard runners are free for a public repo)
Does not address the per-test cost

hypotheses.name: Raise the cold-build test-group concurrency cap
hypotheses.experiment: Evidence from .config/nextest.toml (soldr#3138/#3161): +19% total test-seconds when the group went 2-wide; route-ceiling races.
cons: Treats the symptom of H4; contention tax; flake risk
hypotheses.verdict: REJECT; revisit the cap after H4.

hypotheses.name: Content-skip remote Rust jobs for PRs that cannot affect them
hypotheses.experiment: Reuses E2: 22/80 PRs touch no Rust-test input.
cons: Subsumed by H1 for eligible PRs; for ineligible PRs the changed file is exactly what the remote job must validate
hypotheses.verdict: SUBSUMED by H1 (path-selection keeps the docs-only case).

rounds.design: #190 as filed: attested PR heads skip Lint and Linux x64; any change under .github/workflows/** or to the gate files is ineligible; post-merge run optional; audit sample keyed by PR number.

attacks.attack: Eligibility: how many PRs actually qualify?
attacks.evidence: E1: only 53/80 (66%); 23 more are blocked by edits to workflows the skipped jobs never run (release-auto.yml, benchmark-stats.yml, cook-size-gate.yml ...), which the remote Lint/Linux x64 runs would not validate either.
attacks.change: Surfaces become the closure of what the skipped jobs depend on: their workflow files, local reusable workflows/actions they reference (transitively), the gate declaration, files named in the gate's argv, and declared scripts. -> 62/80 (78%).

attacks.attack: Linux x64 is not a GATE-001 mirror; skipping it drops CI-only probes.
attacks.evidence: No CI-only step failed in 197 runs; all Linux x64 failures were the ci-test step, which the rust/ci-lint/tests lanes run locally.
attacks.change: A non-mirror skip job must declare `covered-by` lanes (reviewable claim, statically checked) and its CI-only scripts become surfaces; the post-merge run keeps the probes.

attacks.attack: A PR can weaken its own gate and attest against the weaker one.
attacks.evidence: Design flaw: verify reads local-gate.toml from the head checkout.
attacks.change: Policy (opt-in, lanes, surfaces) is read from the base commit; lane provenance in the trailer must cover every base-declared lane.

rounds.design: Round 1 + refined surfaces + base-branch policy + covered-by.

attacks.attack: Is the release gate alone an adequate catch-all?
attacks.evidence: E1: before the gate, 9 main breakages in one day, each found by the main push run, not the release; releases are batched, so a release-only catch lets breakage accumulate across many merges.
attacks.change: The default-branch push run is mandatory: verify never trusts a non-PR event, and the static check fails a skip workflow with no push trigger. Release stays the final gate.

attacks.attack: GEN-021 verified reuse would treat a skipped PR run as proof and skip main too.
attacks.evidence: reuse-check requires every required job to conclude `success`; a skipped job concludes `skipped`.
attacks.change: No change needed; documented and covered by reuse-check's existing `required-job-not-success`.

attacks.attack: GitHub's 'Update branch' merge commit is accepted by GATE-003 via its attested first parent.
attacks.evidence: Its tree contains base changes the gate never ran together with this PR's changes.
attacks.change: Trust requires state == attested (exact tree); attested-parent runs remotely.

attacks.attack: Audit sample keyed by PR number lets a PR be permanently in or out.
attacks.change: Key by head SHA: each push is a fresh 1-in-N draw; a rerun of the same head is stable.

rounds.design: Round 2 + mandatory post-merge run + exact attestation + per-head audit.

attacks.evidence: A disagreement in the sample is a real remote failure on that head.
attacks.change: The audit sample simply runs the jobs (blocking). No separate shadow path; `mode = shadow` exists for rollout only.

attacks.evidence: Untrusted authors cannot be held to an honesty contract; ci-full asks for the full matrix.
attacks.change: author_association must be OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, head repo == base repo, and full labels force the run.

attacks.attack: What if the base history is not fetched?
attacks.change: Fail closed (`base-unavailable`); the pilot fetches full history (fetch-depth: 0).

attacks.attack: Without branch protection, nothing stops merging before CI mode finishes.
attacks.evidence: soldr main has no protection or rulesets; 14/75 pre-gate merges had no green run.
attacks.change: Out of scope for the rule, but with trust the decisive checks finish in ~1 min, so waiting for them is cheap; requiring `CI mode` + `Lint` via a ruleset is recommended (repository setting; owner action).

attacks.attack: Does trust move the bottleneck to the developer?
attacks.evidence: Local gate on a Rust change ~498 s (GATE-007 measured); the remote job it replaces is ~650 s plus queueing, after the local run.
attacks.change: Net win on every eligible PR; H4/H2 remain the levers for the local tests lane.

final_design.summary: On an opted-in repository, `ci-lint local-gate verify --trust` in the verify job outputs trusted=true only for a pull_request head that is attested for its exact tree, whose trailer covers every lane the BASE declaration names, from a same-repository author with write access, with no full label, not in the 1-in-N audit sample, and whose merge-base diff touches no trust surface; the declared skip jobs consume that output in their job-level if:. Pushes, schedules and dispatches never skip: the default-branch push runs the jobs for real, and the release candidate's exact-SHA full run is the final gate.
deferred: H2 (#191, multi-crate repositories; per-test recording only with shadow evidence)
rejected: H5 (sharding, unless main/release test stages stay > ~4 min after H4)
final_design.expected_effect_soldr: eligible ordinary PRs (~78%): critical path ~914 s median -> ~60 s; remaining PRs unchanged until H4 lands (~11.5 -> ~7 min estimated)
